title: Leave Kirtland’s property behind, for property is little to God
setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation at Far West, Missouri, on 8 July 1838. It was one of five he dictated that Sunday about Church leaders and finances. William Marks presided over the Church in Kirtland, Ohio, and handled debts for Joseph and Sidney Rigdon. Newel K. Whitney was the Kirtland bishop. Oliver Granger, a Church agent, had probably just arrived from Kirtland with news.
summary: The revelation tells William Marks and Bishop Whitney to settle their business and leave Kirtland before winter. It warns that delay will not go well for them. It asks them to repent of covetous desires and asks, “what is property unto me?” The Kirtland properties may go to pay debts. The voice points to Adam-ondi-Ahman as land with room enough. Marks is to preside at Far West, and Whitney is to be a bishop at Adam-ondi-Ahman after turning from his “littleness of soul”. Oliver Granger is to work for the First Presidency’s redemption, and his name will be held in sacred remembrance. He is to come to Zion and in time become a merchant for the Lord’s people. Last, the Kirtland members are told to keep the Lord’s house holy.

contextNote.title: Sacrifice that counts more than gain
contextNote.text: Oliver Granger was sent back to Kirtland to settle the First Presidency’s debts, a hard and uncertain task. Verse 13 tells him to contend for “the redemption of the First Presidency”. It also expects setbacks: “when he falls he shall rise again”. The reason given is that his sacrifice is “more sacred” than his increase. Verse 4 sets up this contrast by asking what property means to God. In this passage, sacrifice means faithful effort valued apart from its financial result.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 115–120 takes its title from verse 13, about Oliver Granger’s sacrifice. What do verses 4–8 say about property, and how do they change the way verse 13 measures success?
reviewNote: Read all 16 verses. Official heading gives Far West, 8 July 1838, to Marks, Whitney, and Granger. JSP historical introduction read for the five 8 July revelations, Marks as presiding officer and financial agent in Kirtland, Whitney as bishop, Granger probably in Far West with news and sent back as agent. The meaning of the Nicolaitane band is not explained by JSP and is left unexplained here. Fact-check 2026-10-12: summary now covers the closing turns: Granger told to come to Zion and later be a merchant (v. 14), and Kirtland members told to keep the Lord’s house holy (v. 16).
